record.paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
record.context_brief: Contact Fano varieties from Lie theory
record.original_question: For the natural contact Fano varieties obtained as projective bases of conical symplectic singularities arising from Lie theory, is the projective base of a nilpotent orbit closure K-polystable? Is the projective base of a Slodowy slice K-polystable?

evidence.quote:
Problem 23. More precisely,
(1) Is the projective base of a nilpotent orbit closure K-polystable?
(2) Is the projective base of a Slodowy slice K-polystable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A normal complex projective variety $X$ with at worst klt singularities and ample anticanonical class $-K_X$ is called a Fano variety. Such an $X$ is said to be K-polystable if for every test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L}) \to \mathbb{A}^1$ of $(X,-K_X)$ with reduced central fiber, the generalized Donaldson–Futaki invariant satisfies $\mathrm{DF}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L}) \geq 0$, with equality only when the test configuration is a product configuration.

A normal complex affine variety $Y$ with a $\mathbb{C}^*$-action and a holomorphic symplectic form $\omega$ on its smooth locus is called a conical symplectic singularity if (i) the $\mathbb{C}^*$-action contracts $Y$ to a single fixed point $0 \in Y$ and acts on $\omega$ with a positive weight $\ell$, and (ii) $\omega$ extends to a regular (possibly degenerate) $2$-form on any resolution of singularities of $Y$. The projective base of such a conical symplectic singularity $Y$ is the GIT quotient $\mathbb{P}(Y) := (Y \setminus \{0\})/\mathbb{C}^*$; under suitable conditions $\mathbb{P}(Y)$ is a Fano variety and carries a natural contact structure on its smooth locus.

Two natural classes of conical symplectic singularities arise from complex semisimple Lie theory:
(a) Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathfrak{g}$ be a nilpotent (co)adjoint orbit. The orbit closure $\overline{\mathcal{O}} \subset \mathfrak{g}$, with the standard $\mathbb{C}^*$-scaling action, is a conical symplectic singularity.
(b) For a nilpotent element $e \in \mathfrak{g}$ embedded in an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple $(e,h,f)$, the Slodowy slice $\mathcal{S}_e := e + \mathfrak{g}^f$ inherits, after intersecting with a nilpotent orbit closure $\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ containing $e$, a conical symplectic singularity structure (with the Kazhdan $\mathbb{C}^*$-action).

Question. For each of the following, decide whether the resulting contact Fano projective base is K-polystable:
(1) Is the projective base $\mathbb{P}(\overline{\mathcal{O}})$ of a nilpotent orbit closure $\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ in a complex semisimple Lie algebra K-polystable?
(2) Is the projective base $\mathbb{P}(\overline{\mathcal{O}} \cap \mathcal{S}_e)$ of a Slodowy slice in a nilpotent orbit closure K-polystable?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The questions sit within the broader LeBrun–Salamon-type conjecture that contact Fano manifolds/varieties should be K-polystable, an active research area; available literature discusses singularities, resolutions, and K-stability of Fano varieties more generally, but does not establish K-polystability of the projective bases of nilpotent orbit closures or of Slodowy slices in this generality.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of Fano varieties - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A smooth Fano manifold is K-polystable iff it admits a Kähler–Einstein metric; extended to singular Fano varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background framework but does not resolve the specific contact-Fano K-polystability questions.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of Fano varieties: an algebro-geometric approach
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of K-stability for Fano varieties.
status_evidence.claim: General survey; the specific contact Fano cases from Lie theory are not addressed as solved.

status_evidence.title: Resolutions of nilpotent orbit closures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies resolutions and singularities of nilpotent orbit closures.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses geometry of nilpotent orbit closures but not K-polystability of their projective bases.
